excluded.reason: inapplicable: combines only with feature, bug-fix, refactoring, pstack-tdd, not review-fix

master.text: List each finding in the brief with where it is; the parent unit settled the design. Use this workflow for every fix brief that answers a review, a rejected verdict or a landing review, in place of the parent's workflow.

sidekick.text: **Fix the findings the brief lists, inside its Scope, and nothing else.** A review, a rejected verdict or a landing review already found each one; the unit that raised them already settled the design.

1. Read each finding, the code it names, and the parent unit's brief and report. A finding you cannot place, or one whose fix would change the parent's design, goes in the report under Questions; do not redesign around it.

Fix one finding at a time, the smallest change that answers it. Each finding is one commit with the test that pins it, in the same commit, recorded with kitchen.sh step. A finding with no testable behaviour (a comment, a name, a log line) says so in its commit message.
3. Run the brief's Verify commands and the checks each finding names. Nothing in this workflow asks for a failing test committed before its fix.

In the report, under Ran and the sections the template names: each finding with its commit, the test that pins it, and the command output that shows it fixed. A finding left open says why. Every claim carries its command output or a file pointer.

verifier.text: You own the proof, not the fixes. Prove the brief's Acceptance, finding by finding, on the real surface at the unit's head.

Check from the unit's commit range that each listed finding has its commit and the test that pins it, or a commit message saying it has no testable behaviour. A fix brief has no repro-first rule: a test in the same commit as its fix is no finding. Do not write or edit commits.
The evidence standard for the brief's Acceptance, not new criteria: per finding, the command output that shows it fixed at the unit's head. A verdict line cites that output.
